blocks.name: History opening
blocks.contains: Keynes (1930) and Leontief (1983) on work ending; Korinek and Suh, Korinek and Stiglitz, Korinek and Juelfs on AI and wages; what these models leave in the background (what the machine is made of, what life outside work costs).

blocks.name: Two questions and two chains
blocks.contains: The task-margin mechanism; what prices the substitute; what prices the alternative to working; the demand and supply chains back to non-produced inputs; the paper's claim and the George policy pair; the roadmap. Abstract and keywords sit with it.

blocks.name: Description of the economy
blocks.contains: Informal account of the economy: workers, the owner (the parents example), firms and tasks, machines built from machine-hours, labor and land, land as the one non-produced input, the government; what is easy (prices given w and r) and what is hard (the wage-rent ratio).

blocks.name: Primitives, notation, tasks, machines and land
blocks.contains: The list of primitives; Table 1 (notation); Assumptions 1-3 (tasks and the wall H, machines and the user cost, land); the flow benchmark.

blocks.name: The cost system
blocks.contains: Unit costs, the Leontief-Sraffa price system, the cost recursion, price coefficients, the machine-hour's coefficients, prices at the user cost and quantities at the replacement rate.

blocks.name: Workers, the owner and support
blocks.contains: Assumption 4 (workers, the basket, the cost of work), the basket's cost, the budget; Assumption 5 (the owner), its budget, funded support, the dependence benchmark.

blocks.name: Government instruments
blocks.contains: The six instruments (rent tax, wage tax, uniform transfer, payments in work and in exit, public provision of support) and the government budget; task reservation as policy.

blocks.name: Definition of equilibrium and margins
blocks.contains: Definition 1 (stationary equilibrium), its matrix form, premia set aside, Definition 2 (interior margin, boundary assignment, corner), the task-assignment margin.

blocks.name: Two channels of automation
blocks.contains: Definition 3 (task automation, recursive automation), the loom and its makers, AI in the model's terms (computing as machine-hours, datacenters as machines), Trammell and Korinek (2026).

blocks.name: Prices and the task margin
blocks.contains: Lemma 1 (prices and quantities), Proposition 1 (the task margin), Figure 1 (the schedule), the loom example, Restrepo (2025).

blocks.name: Replacement closure
blocks.contains: Proposition 2 (the wage-rent ratio at the margin), the feedback term, the limit as machine services shed labor, Figure 2.

blocks.name: Participation
blocks.contains: Proposition 3 (dependence, living costs and participation), the reservation wage, the strain on support, personal assets, enclosure and common land.

blocks.name: Labor-market clearing, existence and uniqueness
blocks.contains: Labor-market clearing (hours required against hours supplied), Lemma 2 (the ceiling), the margin-indexed prices and quantities, Theorem 1, Corollary 1 (labor supply and the margin).

blocks.name: The real-wage fork and vanishing purchasing power
blocks.contains: The opening summary of results (main.tex L88-90); Proposition 4 (the fork), the human-chain bounds for any network, Caselli and Manning (2019), embodied requirements, Corollary 2 (vanishing wage purchasing power and participation).

blocks.name: Factor income
blocks.contains: Proposition 5 (income identity, bound on labor's share), the instance's shares, Karabarbounis and Neiman, Rognlie, the five statements that change with durable machines.

blocks.name: Rent taxation and a uniform transfer
blocks.contains: Terminal inputs, Proposition 6, the coverage ratio and the rent tax that funds the basket, the measured coverage against the model, Corollary 3 (fiscal capacity as wage income vanishes), the lilies, Korinek and Lockwood (2026).

blocks.name: Numerical economy and automation path
blocks.contains: Table 2 (parameters and targets), the solution, Figure 3 (labor-market clearing under both channels), the automation path along which participation falls to 0.018 and an hour buys 1/426 as much space.

blocks.name: Measurement
blocks.contains: The fork in U.S. wages (4.8 over 1964-2024, Figure 5), the coverage ratio (0.30 in 2025, Figure 6), financing against production (69.6 against 48.9 percent in 2004, Figure 7).

blocks.name: History as four configurations
blocks.contains: Heterogeneity and skill premia, Figure 4, pre-industrial, industrial, post-industrial and AI configurations, the trained-entrant wage ratio.

blocks.name: Possible stabilizers
blocks.contains: Human-required tasks, reservation by law, supply expansion, substitution between services, the wage-premium wedge of Acemoglu and Restrepo (2026).

blocks.name: Artificial intelligence and conclusion
blocks.contains: Both channels and purchasing power, participation, Leontief's horses and the rent dividend, the conjecture on wage-financed consumption, the classical economists, George and Keynes.

blocks.name: Future work
blocks.contains: A dynamic extension, richer participation, the tax mix, a society that no longer organizes itself around paid work.

blocks.name: Toy economy (new)
blocks.contains: A small economy solved by hand before the general model: a few tasks, machines built from labor and land that last one period (the flow benchmark), fixed land and a fixed basket; the task margin, the wage-rent ratio and the participation choice with round numbers.

blocks.name: Related literature (new)
blocks.contains: A section built from the original's cut Section 2 (marginal product, search and bargaining, task models, institutions, the classical accounts, automation and the wage, empirical measures), shortened and updated to the papers the rewrite's introduction cites.

blocks.name: Contributions list (new)
blocks.contains: A numbered list of the paper's contributions in the introduction, each pointing to the result that establishes it.

blocks.name: Facts and the results that read them (new)
blocks.contains: A short table pairing each measured fact (the fork, coverage, financing against production, the labor share and housing) with the proposition that reads it.

blocks.name: Fiscal transition (from Appendix D)
blocks.contains: Conditionality, payroll-tax incidence and schedule slope, the coverage ratio and the basket's requirements, dependence and fiscal coverage, financing the transition and the index D. New to the main text.

blocks.name: Production networks (from Appendix B)
blocks.contains: Any production network with a choice among methods, several non-produced inputs, and the main results restated for them; proofs stay in the appendix. New to the main text.

blocks.name: Human-required tasks (from Appendix E)
blocks.contains: Tasks machines cannot hold, the separate wage on them, Baumol concentration of labor income in those tasks while most workers stay exposed. New to the main text.

blocks.name: The two chains as a figure (new)
blocks.contains: A figure drawing both chains from the labor margin back to non-produced inputs through the cost system, with the machine substitute on one side and the basket on the other.

blocks.name: Financing and production shares (from Appendix F)
blocks.contains: The definitions and construction of the labor-origin financing share and the full-chain human-effort share; bounds and data sources stay in the appendix. New to the main text.

structures.name: The rewrite
structures.idea: Describe the economy, define its equilibrium and characterize it, then derive the results, solve the example, and end with the evidence and the history.

C, expenditure shares under substitution. D, fiscal transition while labor remains employed. E, human-required tasks. F, the financing and production accounts.
